newsitem.title: UK: CIS aluminium exports to fall in 1997 - Macquarie.
newsitem.headline: CIS aluminium exports to fall in 1997 - Macquarie.

text.p: Primary aluminium exports from the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) are forecast to fall to 2.402 million tonnes in 1997, down five percent from the 2.517 million likely to be exported in 1996, Macquarie Equities said.

"We expect 1997 to bring a reduction in primary aluminium exports due to an end to producer de-stocking of primary, and, more importantly, a pick-up in shipments to domestic semi-fabricators," Macquarie said in a weekly commodity report.
Internal CIS consumption is expected to rise to 750,000 tonnes of aluminium next year from 650,000 tonnes in 1996.
Macquarie also forecast exports of semi-fabricated aluminium products to rise to 250,000 tonnes next year from 180,000 tonnes this year.
Elsewhere in the report, Macquarie said it expected around 300,000 tonnes of idled aluminium production capacity to be re-started in 1997.
"However, if demand does not pick up as strongly as we expect, these restarts are likely to be pushed back further," the report said.
Macquarie expected Western world demand to increase 4.3 percent in 1997 from 1996 levels.
The report estimated total idled aluminium smelting capacity at 1.053 million tonnes, around 60 percent of which has costs above the current LME three month price ($1,424/tonne).
However, producers have said market stocks and the level of demand were more important factors when looking at capacity reactivation than the price, Macquarie said.
